newsitem.title: JAPAN: NEC to raise 64MB DRAM output to 4 mln units/mth.
newsitem.headline: NEC to raise 64MB DRAM output to 4 mln units/mth.

text.p: NEC Corp said on Thursday it would increase its output of 64 megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips to four million units a month by the end of March 1998, up from a planned three million units a month by the end of calendar 1997.
NEC's wholly owned unit NEC Semiconductors (UK) Ltd in Scotland will boost production to achieve the planned increase, a company spokesman said.
NEC plans to invest 40 billion yen in the unit in the year from April 1, 1997, with part of that amount to be used for the increase in 64-MB DRAM chip output, he said.
NEC plans 190 billion yen in capital investment in semiconductor operations in 1997/98, including the 40 billion yen for the Scottish unit, the spokesman said.
